items.title: Families clear homes of David Walliams books after sexual offence allegations

Her children, aged eight, six and four, have dressed up as his characters for World Book Day – they love the over-the-top, unusual names and illustrations. Now, all the books are going. “I’ll probably take them away and replace them with other authors,” says Sarah, a mother in west London. “Sooner rather than later, so they don’t realise.” If any of her children ask why, she will tell them “that his choices aren’t great and that I think we should be reading other books”. items.title: A global Microsoft 365 outage has hit millions – what happened and when will it be fixed?
items.desc: Problem affects businesses, government agencies and even tech firm’s own employees Microsoft scrambles to fix global outage affecting Teams and Outlook Microsoft outage – live updates Tell us: have you been affected by the Microsoft outage? Millions of people were unable to access their emails, Teams chats or meetings on Thursday night and Friday after a Microsoft 365 outage brought down services across the globe. The outage has lasted for more than 21 hours, with meaningful signs of recovery visible beginning shortly before midday GMT on Friday. It affected businesses, government agencies and even Microsoft employees all over the world. Those reporting issues have included the US House of Representatives, an Australian spy agency, airlines in India, European government agencies, and police services, ambulances and hospitals in the UK. Continue reading...
